## Observed Pattern (full-sprint dataset: 11 dispatches)

| Batch | Dispatch mode | Size | Agents (type) | Leaked |
|-------|---------------|------|---------------|--------|
| 1 | PARALLEL (one message) | 4 | 315a(gp), 5e96(gp), 55c7(red-test-writer), b5fd(red-test-writer) | b5fd (4th) |
| 2 | PARALLEL (one message) | 3 | 2298(gp), 3da3(gp), 71bb(gp) | 3da3 (2nd) |
| 3 | PARALLEL (one message) | 2 | 4268(gp), 6f49(gp) | 4268 (1st) |
| 4 | SOLO (one agent) | 1 | ef64(gp) | none |
| 5 | SOLO (re-dispatch) | 1 | ef64(gp) | none |

### The pattern: concurrency, not agent type
- **Every parallel (same-message) batch leaked EXACTLY ONE agent** — 1 of 4, 1 of 3, 1 of 2. The "exactly one per batch regardless of batch size" signal strongly suggests a race in the harness's concurrent worktree provisioning where exactly one of the simultaneous allocations fails to materialize an isolated worktree (the agent then falls back to the session CWD).
- **Both SOLO dispatches isolated cleanly (0 leaks of 2).** No leak ever occurred when only one isolation:worktree agent was provisioned at a time.
- **No agent-type correlation:** red-test-writer leaked 1/2 and succeeded 1/2; general-purpose leaked 2/9 and succeeded 7/9. Both types both leaked and succeeded.
- **No dispatch-order correlation:** the leaked agent was the 4th, then the 2nd, then the 1st in its batch — not a fixed position.

### Conclusion
There IS an observable pattern: leaks correlate with **concurrent multi-agent dispatch in a single message**, not with agent type, model, or task. Solo dispatch was 100% reliable (2/2); every concurrent batch produced exactly one isolation failure (3/3 batches).

### Actionable mitigations to evaluate
1. Workaround available today: dispatch isolation:worktree agents ONE AT A TIME (solo) — eliminates the race at the cost of parallelism.
2. Or keep parallel dispatch + add the orchestrator-side post-dispatch verification already used here: check each completion notification for a <worktree> block and cross-check `git worktree list`; on a miss, recover via the RECOVERED_FROM_SESSION path. (3/3 leaks recovered with zero data loss this way.)
3. Upstream (Claude Code): the concurrent-provisioning path appears to have a one-loser race; capture harness version on next recurrence and file upstream with this dataset.
